headline: Transposable elements supply new miRNA target sites and alternative exons
label: Transposon Driven Regulatory Evolution
summary: January 2026 items converge on transposons and splicing as sources of regulatory variation across plant and animal genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread treats mobile and repetitive sequence, and the chromatin and splicing contexts that read it, as sources of regulatory variation rather than noise. Across eight Oryza AA-genome species, transposable element insertions create new miRNA target sites that expand the plant miRNA regulatory network. In the Drosophila brain, improved TEChim software is used to argue that transposon insertions act as alternative exons, a claim offered as a rebuttal to Azad et al. A separate hematopoiesis study curates transcriptomes across six vertebrates and uses FAScore, an ML model with 19 features, to predict functional exon skipping. A chromatin-state analysis in Arabidopsis and Marchantia finds conservation over 450 million years of land plant evolution and links states to transcription factor accessibility. What is new is the convergence of TE-derived sequence on both miRNA target and exon definition, together with feature-based and state-based annotation of regulatory function across deep evolutionary distances.
